entry.summary: A US territory: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program, as for the mainland, under 90 days.

sources.title: United States of America travel advice
sources.supports: the Visa Waiver Program covers the US and its territories, including the US Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico

tourism.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
tourism.detail: Tourism under 90 days. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

meetings.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
meetings.detail: Consulting with business associates is a permitted activity. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.
meetings.next: Be ready to explain the purpose at the border.

conference.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
conference.detail: Attending professional conferences is permitted. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

unpaid-speaking.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
unpaid-speaking.detail: Speaking at a conference without payment is generally a business visit; officers decide at the border. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.
unpaid-speaking.next: Carry the invitation showing no payment beyond expenses.

paid-speaking.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program (honorarium rules)
paid-speaking.detail: Speaking fees are allowed only from qualifying (mainly academic or nonprofit research) institutions, for no more than nine days at one institution and from no more than five institutions in six months; no salary from a US entity. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.
paid-speaking.next: Check the payer qualifies; otherwise a work visa is needed.

book-launch.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program or a work visa
book-launch.detail: Promotion and readings may be business activity; paid appearances fall under the honorarium limits. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.
book-launch.next: Ask a US Embassy or an immigration lawyer.

ai-teaching.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program (honorarium rules) or a work visa
ai-teaching.detail: Academic lectures can fit the honorarium rules; paid teaching for a company needs a work visa. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

remote-work.route: Not addressed for visitors (US immigration law)
remote-work.detail: Visitors (ESTA or B visa) may not take employment; the State Department pages list meetings, conferences and negotiations but do not address remote work for a foreign employer either way.
remote-work.next: Ask US Customs and Border Protection or a US consulate in writing.

sources.supports: permitted business activities (read via a search-index snapshot)

entrepreneur.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
entrepreneur.detail: Negotiating contracts and meeting partners fit; working in a US business needs a visa. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

trade.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
trade.detail: Contract negotiation is a permitted activity. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

artist.route: Performer visa (for example O or P)
artist.detail: Only amateurs taking part unpaid in musical or similar events fit the waiver. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

mixed-mission.detail: The waiver covers business visits only; any work needs a visa. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

filming.route: Media (I) visa for foreign media work
filming.detail: Representatives of foreign film or other information media are excluded from B-1 business visits. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.
filming.next: Ask a US Embassy which visa fits the filming you plan.

research.route: B-1 or ESTA for independent research (US law applies)
research.detail: US immigration law applies here: independent, unpaid research benefiting no US institution is a permitted B-1 activity.

sources.title: 9 FAM 402.2

volunteering.detail: Smartraveller notes that volunteering isn't allowed under the Visa Waiver Program. US immigration law applies in Puerto Rico.

laws.rule: Puerto Rico allows cannabis only for authorised medical use under Law 42-2017 (Ley MEDICINAL), with a physician's recommendation and the required ID; recreational use is not permitted. US federal law also applies.
